behavioral_notes.observation: The default online_redirect flow (gap #7) builds a Checkout Pro 'preference' via _mercado_pago_prepare_preference_request_payload (items[] with reference/amount/currency, payer name/email/phone/address, auto_return='all', back_urls all pointing at /payment/mercado_pago/return, external_reference=tx.reference, notification_url=/payment/mercado_pago/webhook/<url-quoted reference>, statement_descriptor=company name) and POSTs it to '/checkout/preferences' through payment.provider._send_api_request. It reads response['init_point'] when provider.state=='enabled' else response['sandbox_init_point'], then parses that hosted-checkout URL and re-embeds its query params as hidden inputs in the redirect form so the buyer is bounced to Mercado Pago's hosted page. Amounts are normalized by _mercado_pago_convert_amount, which rounds DOWN to const.CURRENCY_DECIMALS (COP/HNL/NIO are 0-decimal, deviating from ISO 4217) else payment's CURRENCY_MINOR_UNITS. None of this server-to-server HTTP or the sandbox/live URL switch is visible in Python field/model metadata.

Two direct-API paths bypass the redirect. (1) The public jsonrpc controller route /payment/mercado_pago/payments receives the card token/installments/brand/issuer from the browser SDK, resolves the tx via _search_by_reference, builds the base payload, POSTs '/v1/payments' with an idempotency key (scope='direct_payment'), then _process('mercado_pago', ...). (2) payment.transaction._send_payment_request (off-session token charge) first POSTs '/v1/card_tokens' with the saved card_id to mint a fresh single-use token, then POSTs '/v1/payments' (transaction_amount, token, installments=1, payer.id=token.mercado_pago_customer_id) with idempotency key scope='token_payment' and _process()es the result. Both reuse _mercado_pago_prepare_base_request_payload (external_reference, notification_url, statement_descriptor). The per-charge card_tokens round-trip and the idempotency-key scoping are invisible to metadata.

Mercado Pago has no signed-webhook scheme, so settlement is verified by an authenticated callback GET rather than an HMAC. The redirect-return route /payment/mercado_pago/return (GET, public) and the webhook /payment/mercado_pago/webhook/<path:reference> (POST, public, csrf=False) both funnel into _verify_and_process: it _search_by_reference's the tx, then GETs '/v1/payments/<payment_id>' from api.mercadopago.com (Bearer access-token auth) to fetch authoritative payment data and only then calls tx_sudo._process('mercado_pago', verified_data). The webhook filters out IPNs (it only acts when data['action'] is 'payment.created'/'payment.updated', since IPNs leave 'action' empty); the return route skips processing when payment_id=='null' (buyer cancelled). The trust boundary is the server-to-server verification GET, not the inbound request itself.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates -> status mapping into payment's state machine
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates stamps provider_reference = payment_data['id'], maps payment_type_id/payment_method_id through const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING (falling back to the 'unknown' payment.method), then translates Mercado Pago's status via const.TRANSACTION_STATUS_MAPPING into payment's guarded transitions: pending/in_process/in_mediation/authorized -> _set_pending; approved/refunded -> _set_done; cancelled/null -> _set_canceled; rejected -> _set_error (with a human message from const.ERROR_MESSAGE_MAPPING keyed on status_detail); any other status -> _set_error. _extract_amount_data and _extract_reference read amount/currency/external_reference back from the verified payload. This inbound status->state translation is pure code semantics, not derivable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: OAuth onboarding via odoo proxy (action_start_onboarding / _mercado_pago_fetch_access_token / MercadoPagoOnboardingController)
behavioral_notes.observation: Onboarding is OAuth-by-proxy, not direct API-key entry. action_start_onboarding (override) gates on const.SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES (RedirectWarning if the company country is unsupported), requires an account country, then redirects (ir.actions.act_url) to the Mercado Pago authorize URL built through Odoo's proxy at https://mercadopago.api.odoo.com/api/mercado_pago/1 (is_proxy_request=True), carrying a return_url to /payment/mercado_pago/oauth/return plus a csrf_token. The oauth/return controller (auth=user) validates the CSRF token (Forbidden on failure), POSTs '/get_access_token' through the proxy to exchange the authorization_code, and writes mercado_pago_access_token/refresh_token/public_key + flips the provider to state='enabled', is_published=True, allow_tokenization=True, then syncs currency. _mercado_pago_fetch_access_token transparently refreshes an expired token by POSTing '/refresh_access_token' through the proxy (expiry is backdated 31 days so refresh happens before the refresh token dies). @api.constrains block enabling without an access token and tokenization without a public key. All of this OAuth/proxy choreography is invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, OAuth keys, SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; two outbound endpoints -- https://api.mercadopago.com (direct REST, Bearer access-token auth: /checkout/preferences, /v1/payments, /v1/card_tokens, /v1/customers[/search][/<id>/cards]) and https://mercadopago.api.odoo.com/api/mercado_pago (Odoo's Mercado Pago OAuth proxy: /authorize, /get_access_token, /refresh_access_token, jsonrpc) -- declared in const.py and models/payment_provider.py. No 'requests' import here: HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine, which payment_mercado_pago configures via the _build_request_url / _build_request_headers / _parse_response_content / _parse_response_error hook overrides (headers add X-Platform-Id, X-Idempotency-Key, and the Bearer access token). On the browser side the Mercado Pago JS SDK is loaded on payment-form pages (PaymentForm.prototype patch) to tokenize the card client-side before the /payment/mercado_pago/payments jsonrpc call. This dual server-to-server + client-side acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (static) -- Mercado Pago SDK inline form patch
behavioral_notes.observation: 1 JS file, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds (gap #3). The module patches the shared PaymentForm widget (static/src/interactions/payment_form.js -> PaymentForm.prototype) rather than registering a new component: it consumes the inline-form values JSON from payment.provider._mercado_pago_get_inline_form_values (buyer email + mercado_pago_public_key) to mount the Mercado Pago JS SDK, tokenize the card in-browser, and POST the resulting token/installments/brand/issuer to the public jsonrpc route /payment/mercado_pago/payments. Assets load into web.assets_frontend (manifest glob static/src/**/*). These browser interactions and the Mercado Pago SDK are invisible to Python metadata (gap #3).

external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration for Latin America. Outbound server-to-server REST to api.mercadopago.com (Checkout Pro /checkout/preferences, /v1/payments, /v1/card_tokens, /v1/customers + cards) authenticated with an OAuth access token; merchant onboarding routed through Odoo's mercadopago.api.odoo.com OAuth proxy (authorize / get_access_token / refresh_access_token); a parallel client-side Mercado Pago JS SDK tokenization channel; and inbound settlement via a redirect-return route plus a csrf=False webhook, both verified by an authenticated GET /v1/payments/<id> (no HMAC signature scheme -- the trust boundary is the verification call, unlike Stripe's signed webhook).
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Mercado Pago endpoints, the OAuth Bearer auth + proxy onboarding, the verification-GET trust model, or the browser SDK channel are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading const.py + the model/controller code.

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_mercado_pago is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the Latin-American cardholder/wallet holder and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Mercado Pago's payment network. It exhibits the three mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (OAuth self-onboarding through the Odoo proxy, per-country eligibility and currency binding, token/key management), service provisioning (creating the Checkout Pro preference or the direct /v1/payments charge and verifying settlement per transaction), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.mercadopago.com link, the client-side Mercado Pago JS SDK channel, and the verify-GET-based return/webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Mercado Pago realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe.metamodel.json (network/support) and the parent payment engine; it differs from Stripe mainly in the trust model (an authenticated verification GET rather than a signed webhook) and in OAuth-by-proxy onboarding rather than Connect.
classification.apqc_evidence: apqc_odoo_map.tsv: '9.5.x process accounts payable (pay) -> account.payment register payment -> support'; payment acceptance feeds that collect-cash process upstream of the ledger.

country support is bounded by const.SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES (AR/BR/CL/CO/MX/PE/UY); other LatAm regions cannot onboard
full OAuth proxy request/response contract (mercadopago.api.odoo.com) is opaque -- onboarding depends on Odoo's IAP proxy being reachable
installments fixed to 1 for token/off-session charges; richer installment plans only via the in-browser SDK path
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here
